Supply chain due diligence

Shared sub-tier supplier screening

Report scope

Screened supplier list. Shared upstream entities are observed within retrieved evidence.

Report content generated: 24 September 2026, 01:52 UTC

Terms and definitions

  • Entity: a person or organisation represented by a Sayari record.
  • Match strength: Sayari's assessment of how well an input matches a record; weak matches are not accepted identities.
  • Upstream: entities found earlier in a supplier's trade network within the search limits.
  • Tier: Sayari's annotation of an entity's position along a retrieved trade path. The screened supplier is Tier 1, so the first step shown on a supply chain path is Tier 2, and the configured search depth limits how far upstream the tiers reach. This report does not recalculate it.
  • Risk factor: a named signal reported by Sayari for an entity or its connections, not a complete risk assessment.
  • Seed risk: Sayari describes “direct associations between entities and authoritative risk sources”. Some are country indicators rather than allegations about the entity itself.
  • Network risk: Sayari describes “risk exposure through business relationships, ownership structures, and trading activity”.
  • PSA risk (Possibly-Same-As): Sayari describes “potential risk through entity similarities that suggest a relationship but lack definitive proof”; a PSA factor concerns another entity in the same possible-identity group, not confirmed risk on this entity.
  • Level: Sayari's severity label on a reported factor; the report's selection rules are separate.
  • Shared sub-tier supplier: an entity found upstream of more than one screened supplier; the connection is trade-record evidence, not proof of direct supply.
  • HS code: a Harmonized System product classification code attached to a trade record.

Factor names and definitions come from Sayari’s published ontology snapshot. Where a factor is not in that snapshot, the report shows Sayari’s original identifier for it instead of a name. Those identifiers also appear in the data export, so every factor can be traced back to Sayari.

Terminology source: Sayari documentation, API guides, Risk factors — documentation.sayari.com/api/guides/risk-factors.

Coverage and data completeness

This section shows how much supplier data was successfully matched and analyzed. Records that could not be matched, and separate records that map to the same legal entity, both make the number of uploaded supplier records differ from the number of unique entities analyzed.

Screened supplier list

  • Fully assessed 16Upstream evidence was found; Sayari did not flag the search as partial. The result limit counts supply chain paths, not entities. Entities along those paths can outnumber the path limit. A search can stop at the path limit without being flagged as partial.
  • Partially assessed 16Some upstream evidence was retrieved, but the available information may be incomplete.
  • No upstream data found 14The lookup completed successfully, but no upstream relationships were returned.
  • Retrieval issue 0Upstream data could not be retrieved successfully.
  • Not assessed 4Upstream analysis was not performed because a sufficiently reliable supplier match was not available.

Some suppliers could not be fully analyzed because they could not be matched to a company record, or because Sayari flagged the upstream search as partial. These cases are shown separately so that missing information is not interpreted as an absence of risk. Suppliers with uncertain matches or incomplete evidence may require additional review. Where a company profile was unavailable, that supplier’s risk factors are unknown rather than absent.

Suppliers requiring additional review

Each supplier below is missing something the analysis needed. None of these is a result of “no findings”: the check did not run or did not complete. Confirming a match needs enough identifying detail to tell one company from another, and a registered legal name or company identifier is usually what settles it.

  • Denso — No sufficiently reliable entity match was identified. Additional supplier details may be required to continue the analysis.
  • Dana — No sufficiently reliable entity match was identified. Additional supplier details may be required to continue the analysis.
  • HELLA — Possible entity match identified, but confidence was not high enough for automated analysis. Manual review recommended.

How shared upstream entities were selected

Each step narrows the upstream entities found for the screened suppliers down to the entities listed under Shared upstream entities flagged for review. Counts are lower bounds within retrieved evidence, and an entity removed by a step is not an entity found to be free of risk. Methodology and limitations explains the country limit used to select entities.

Screened supplier list — selection steps

Selection stepCountWhat this means
Matched suppliers with upstream trade evidence32Suppliers matched to a Sayari company record whose upstream trade search returned at least one entity.
Upstream entities identified8628Every distinct entity reached by the upstream trade search within the configured depth and result limit. A lower bound, not the whole network.
Upstream entities shared by more than one supplier848Entities appearing upstream of at least two matched suppliers on this list. The connection is trade-record evidence, not proof of a direct supply relationship.
Excluded — associated with too many countries300Entities above the country limit stated in Methodology and limitations. These are typically logistics providers, trading intermediaries or large distributors, which would crowd the ranking without distinguishing between suppliers. Excluded from ranking only.
Shared entities within the country limit548The shared entities carried into the risk factor rules.
Excluded — no critical or high risk factor419Entities with no Sayari risk factor published at critical or high level. This is not a finding of no risk.
Shared entities flagged for review129Entities meeting both the country limit and the risk factor rules. These are the entities listed under Shared upstream entities flagged for review.

Risk factors identified

Some of these factors may rest on a company match Sayari has not confirmed. Treat them as signals to review alongside the evidence, not as confirmed findings.

  • Indirect Exports of Critical Components in USA Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) Common High Priority Items ListNetwork riskhigh The entity may have been involved, knowingly or unknowingly, in indirect exports to Russia, Belarus, or Iran through intermediate countries (2-3 hops away) of shipments with Harmonized System (HS) codes corresponding to critical U.S. components that Russia relies on for its weapons systems. These HS codes listed in Tier 1 and Tier 2 of the U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security's Common High Priority List (CHPL) are subject to the most comprehensive controls under the Export Administration Regulations (15 CFR Parts 730 – 774) (EAR). The BIS has developed the CHPL in collaboration with the European Union, Japan, and the United Kingdom.
  • Imports from USA OFAC Non-SDN Consolidated Sanctions List EntityNetwork riskhigh The entity imports from an entity that has been listed in the USA OFAC Non-SDN Consolidated Sanctions List. This Risk Factor applies only where the relevant shipment departed after the designation date of the listed entity. This does not, by definition, indicate a violation of export control or sanctions law. Imports from listed entities may be permitted under general licenses, exemptions, or based on the item’s classification and intended end use.
  • Imports from Entity in BIS Entity ListNetwork riskhigh Historical shipment records suggest that the entity has imported one or more goods from an entity that has been added to the BIS Entity List.     This entity has a "Medium Risk" ESG Controversy Exposure Score (41-60). Scores are derived from three primary components -- intensity scores, volume scores, and novelty scores. The intensity score measures the severity of each identified ESG incident involving the company, considering its impact on an entity's reputation, stakeholders, financial standing, and legal implications. The volume score assesses the number of articles associated with each event within a short-term rolling window. To ensure accuracy, the volume score is normalized against the average article volume concerning the company and relevant ESG topics over the past year, reducing potential bias. The novelty score accounts for how recent a topic is, weighing them accordingly. News and events related to old topics are discounted, while new topics are assigned heavier weights for a given entity. To see the events that contributed to this score, including ESG subcategory, intensity, and article summaries, please see the associated adverse media records.

  • Medium Risk ESG Controversy Exposure ScoreSeed riskelevated

    Signal reported as present

    This entity has a "Medium Risk" ESG Controversy Exposure Score (41-60). Scores are derived from three primary components -- intensity scores, volume scores, and novelty scores. The intensity score measures the severity of each identified ESG incident involving the company, considering its impact on an entity's reputation, stakeholders, financial standing, and legal implications. The volume score assesses the number of articles associated with each event within a short-term rolling window. To ensure accuracy, the volume score is normalized against the average article volume concerning the company and relevant ESG topics over the past year, reducing potential bias. The novelty score accounts for how recent a topic is, weighing them accordingly. News and events related to old topics are discounted, while new topics are assigned heavier weights for a given entity. To see the events that contributed to this score, including ESG subcategory, intensity, and article summaries, please see the associated adverse media records.

    This entity has a "Medium Risk" ESG Controversy Exposure Score (41-60). Scores are derived from three primary components -- intensity scores, volume scores, and novelty scores. The intensity score measures the severity of each identified ESG incident involving the company, considering its impact on an entity's reputation, stakeholders, financial standing, and legal implications. The volume score assesses the number of articles associated with each event within a short-term rolling window. To ensure accuracy, the volume score is normalized against the average article volume concerning the company and relevant ESG topics over the past year, reducing potential bias. The novelty score accounts for how recent a topic is, weighing them accordingly. News and events related to old topics are discounted, while new topics are assigned heavier weights for a given entity.     Signal reported as present

    This entity has a "Medium Risk" ESG Controversy Exposure Score (41-60). Scores are derived from three primary components -- intensity scores, volume scores, and novelty scores. The intensity score measures the severity of each identified ESG incident involving the company, considering its impact on an entity's reputation, stakeholders, financial standing, and legal implications. The volume score assesses the number of articles associated with each event within a short-term rolling window. To ensure accuracy, the volume score is normalized against the average article volume concerning the company and relevant ESG topics over the past year, reducing potential bias. The novelty score accounts for how recent a topic is, weighing them accordingly. News and events related to old topics are discounted, while new topics are assigned heavier weights for a given entity. To see the events that contributed to this score, including ESG subcategory, intensity, and article summaries, please see the associated adverse media records.

    This entity has a "Medium Risk" ESG Controversy Exposure Score (41-60). Scores are derived from three primary components -- intensity scores, volume scores, and novelty scores. The intensity score measures the severity of each identified ESG incident involving the company, considering its impact on an entity's reputation, stakeholders, financial standing, and legal implications. The volume score assesses the number of articles associated with each event within a short-term rolling window. To ensure accuracy, the volume score is normalized against the average article volume concerning the company and relevant ESG topics over the past year, reducing potential bias. The novelty score accounts for how recent a topic is, weighing them accordingly. News and events related to old topics are discounted, while new topics are assigned heavier weights for a given entity. To see the events that contributed to this score, including ESG subcategory, intensity, and article summaries, please see the associated adverse media records.

    Signal reported as present

    This entity has a "Very High Risk" ESG Controversy Exposure Score (81-100). Scores are derived from three primary components -- intensity scores, volume scores, and novelty scores. The intensity score measures the severity of each identified ESG incident involving the company, considering its impact on an entity's reputation, stakeholders, financial standing, and legal implications. The volume score assesses the number of articles associated with each event within a short-term rolling window. To ensure accuracy, the volume score is normalized against the average article volume concerning the company and relevant ESG topics over the past year, reducing potential bias. The novelty score accounts for how recent a topic is, weighing them accordingly. News and events related to old topics are discounted, while new topics are assigned heavier weights for a given entity. To see the events that contributed to this score, including ESG subcategory, intensity, and article summaries, please see the associated adverse media records.

  • Medium Risk ESG Controversy Exposure ScoreSeed riskelevated

    Signal reported as present

    This entity has a "Medium Risk" ESG Controversy Exposure Score (41-60). Scores are derived from three primary components -- intensity scores, volume scores, and novelty scores. The intensity score measures the severity of each identified ESG incident involving the company, considering its impact on an entity's reputation, stakeholders, financial standing, and legal implications. The volume score assesses the number of articles associated with each event within a short-term rolling window. To ensure accuracy, the volume score is normalized against the average article volume concerning the company and relevant ESG topics over the past year, reducing potential bias. The novelty score accounts for how recent a topic is, weighing them accordingly. News and events related to old topics are discounted, while new topics are assigned heavier weights for a given entity. To see the events that contributed to this score, including ESG subcategory, intensity, and article summaries, please see the associated adverse media records.

  • Medium Risk ESG Controversy Exposure ScoreSeed riskelevated

    Signal reported as present

    This entity has a "Medium Risk" ESG Controversy Exposure Score (41-60). Scores are derived from three primary components -- intensity scores, volume scores, and novelty scores. The intensity score measures the severity of each identified ESG incident involving the company, considering its impact on an entity's reputation, stakeholders, financial standing, and legal implications. The volume score assesses the number of articles associated with each event within a short-term rolling window. To ensure accuracy, the volume score is normalized against the average article volume concerning the company and relevant ESG topics over the past year, reducing potential bias. The novelty score accounts for how recent a topic is, weighing them accordingly. News and events related to old topics are discounted, while new topics are assigned heavier weights for a given entity. To see the events that contributed to this score, including ESG subcategory, intensity, and article summaries, please see the associated adverse media records.

  • Medium Risk ESG Controversy Exposure ScoreSeed riskelevated

    Signal reported as present

    This entity has a "Medium Risk" ESG Controversy Exposure Score (41-60). Scores are derived from three primary components -- intensity scores, volume scores, and novelty scores. The intensity score measures the severity of each identified ESG incident involving the company, considering its impact on an entity's reputation, stakeholders, financial standing, and legal implications. The volume score assesses the number of articles associated with each event within a short-term rolling window. To ensure accuracy, the volume score is normalized against the average article volume concerning the company and relevant ESG topics over the past year, reducing potential bias. The novelty score accounts for how recent a topic is, weighing them accordingly. News and events related to old topics are discounted, while new topics are assigned heavier weights for a given entity. To see the events that contributed to this score, including ESG subcategory, intensity, and article summaries, please see the associated adverse media records.

  • High Risk ESG Controversy Exposure ScoreSeed riskelevated This entity has a "High Risk" ESG Controversy Exposure Score (61-80). Scores are derived from three primary components -- intensity scores, volume scores, and novelty scores. The intensity score measures the severity of each identified ESG incident involving the company, considering its impact on an entity's reputation, stakeholders, financial standing, and legal implications. The volume score assesses the number of articles associated with each event within a short-term rolling window. To ensure accuracy, the volume score is normalized against the average article volume concerning the company and relevant ESG topics over the past year, reducing potential bias. The novelty score accounts for how recent a topic is, weighing them accordingly. News and events related to old topics are discounted, while new topics are assigned heavier weights for a given entity. To see the events that contributed to this score, including ESG subcategory, intensity, and article summaries, please see the associated adverse media records.

The intensity score measures the severity of each identified ESG incident involving the company, considering its impact on an entity's reputation, stakeholders, financial standing, and legal implications. The volume score assesses the number of articles associated with each event within a short-term rolling window. To ensure accuracy, the volume score is normalized against the average article volume concerning the company and relevant ESG topics over the past year, reducing potential bias. The novelty score accounts for how recent a topic is, weighing them accordingly. News and events related to old topics are discounted, while new topics are assigned heavier weights for a given entity. To see the events that contributed to this score, including ESG subcategory, intensity, and article summaries, please see the associated adverse media records.

  • Medium Risk ESG Controversy Exposure ScoreSeed riskelevated This entity has a "Medium Risk" ESG Controversy Exposure Score (41-60). Scores are derived from three primary components -- intensity scores, volume scores, and novelty scores. The intensity score measures the severity of each identified ESG incident involving the company, considering its impact on an entity's reputation, stakeholders, financial standing, and legal implications. The volume score assesses the number of articles associated with each event within a short-term rolling window. To ensure accuracy, the volume score is normalized against the average article volume concerning the company and relevant ESG topics over the past year, reducing potential bias. The novelty score accounts for how recent a topic is, weighing them accordingly. News and events related to old topics are discounted, while new topics are assigned heavier weights for a given entity. To see the events that contributed to this score, including ESG subcategory, intensity, and article summaries, please see the associated adverse media records.

Methodology and limitations

Scope and coverage

  • For each matched supplier, Sayari’s upstream trade network was searched up to 3 steps, returning at most 500 supply chain paths. Entities along those paths can outnumber the path limit. Fully assessed means upstream evidence was found and Sayari did not flag the search as partial. A search can stop at the path limit without being flagged as partial.
  • Every count here is a minimum. It describes what the search returned, not everything that exists, and it is not exhaustive supply-chain coverage.
  • Every supplier is given one of five coverage states — fully assessed, partially assessed, no upstream data found, retrieval issue, or not assessed — each explained beside its count earlier in this report. All five describe what this search retrieved, not what Sayari holds and not what exists: not assessed means no search was run for that supplier, and no state, fully assessed included, means a supplier is free of risk.

Sayari API configuration

  • Every company, connection and risk factor on this page comes from Sayari’s own data, retrieved through the official Sayari Python SDK. Nothing is modelled or estimated, and the only input from outside Sayari is the supplier list that was screened.
  • Three Sayari endpoints are used: resolution to match each supplier to a Sayari identity, entity_summary to read that identity’s profile and risk factors, and upstream_trade_traversal to retrieve its upstream trade network.
  • Each supplier is matched on its name, address and country. Resolution returns one page of at most 10 candidates.
  • The trade search runs to a depth of 3. Tier 1 is the screened supplier itself, so this limit allows paths as far as Tier 4. Displayed tiers retain Sayari’s annotations.
  • Each search returns at most 500 supply chain paths, and at most 6 example paths are kept for each listed entity.

Entity selection criteria

  • An entity is listed when it sits upstream of more than one of the matched suppliers on this list. Entities are ordered by how many suppliers reach them, then by fewest countries.
  • A supply chain path counts for every entity along it, not only the company it ends at. A path that reaches an entity and carries on further upstream is still evidence for that entity.
  • Sayari often returns more paths than this report shows. Examples are taken from each connected supplier in rotation, never ranked, so they cover as many suppliers as possible. Only 6 are kept for each entity, so where more than 6 suppliers reach the same entity, some of them have no example in this report.
  • Each route ends at the entity it is listed under. Where Sayari’s path continued further upstream, the route says so rather than listing the companies beyond that point.
  • Entities present in more than 10 countries are set aside before the risk rules are applied. Entities in many countries are typically logistics providers, trading intermediaries or large distributors: they sit upstream of almost everyone and would crowd out the list without distinguishing between suppliers. This is a screening choice made here, not a Sayari assessment, and it classifies no individual entity.

Risk classification

  • An entity qualifies for review on Sayari’s own published critical and high levels, applied after the country limit above.
  • Elevated and relevant factors appear as context only and never place an entity on this list by themselves. Neither do factors Sayari publishes no definition for, which appear under their original identifiers. Selection never matches on words in a factor’s name.
  • Seed, network and PSA factors keep the risk type Sayari published for them. PSA means “possibly the same as”: a possible match to another Sayari record, never a confirmed one. A factor labelled “Possibly the Same As (PSA)” is itself such a match; one labelled “May Include 'PSA' Path” means the risk path may pass through one. Either way the link is unconfirmed, and network factors keep their network classification.
  • A network value is Sayari’s reported distance to the nearest risk target — not a score, and not the tier numbers shown on trade paths. Values without interpreted units are kept in the findings data and omitted from the displayed value sentences.
